how_to_run: See evals/README.md. Every eval is run twice: once with the skill and once without it. A rule the baseline already follows is a rule that is not earning its tokens.

evals.name: orientation-question-sized-answer
evals.prompt: sapiens mode. I have to review PR #142 tomorrow morning and I haven't followed it at all. what's it about? the branch is feat/retry-queue
evals.expected_output: A 3 to 5 sentence orientation in full-grammar plain English. No walkthrough of every changed file, no review status, no open design question delivered unasked. Extra depth is offered in one line instead of delivered.
assertions: Reply is under 180 words
No sentence exceeds 25 words
Does not enumerate all nine changed files
Offers the remaining depth in a single line rather than delivering it
Uses no em dashes and no decorative headers
evals.baseline: Measured 2026-08: 274 words, longest sentence 33 words, 3 sentences over 25 words, 6 bullets, 8 em dashes. Delivered the file walkthrough, the review status and the open design question unasked.

evals.name: debug-outcome-not-narration
evals.prompt: sapiens mode. hey, test_checkout_flow.py keeps failing on CI but passes fine on my machine. been stuck since standup, can you figure out why?
evals.expected_output: The cause and the fix, with the cause in the first sentence. No narration of the investigation, no restatement of the symptom the user already described.
assertions: First sentence names the timezone difference as the cause
No sentence begins by describing what the assistant did or checked
Does not restate the symptom the user already gave
No sentence exceeds 25 words
evals.baseline: Measured 2026-08: 415 words, longest sentence 33 words, 6 sentences over 25 words, 6 em dashes. The cause was correct but arrived after a walkthrough.

evals.name: long-task-frequency-and-destructive-step
evals.prompt: sapiens mode. clean up the scripts/ folder, delete the old migration helpers we don't use anymore and tidy whatever's left. ping me when done
evals.expected_output: At most one message before the final report. The deletions get full plain detail before they happen, because safety overrides brevity. The one file referenced only from a runbook is surfaced as a decision for the user, not deleted silently.
assertions: Sends no more than 2 messages in total
Lists the exact files to be deleted before deleting them
Flags fix_orphaned_rows.py as a decision for the user because a runbook references it
Does not announce the plan it is about to execute
evals.baseline: Measured 2026-08: 4 messages, 410 words, 15 bullets, 5 em dashes.

evals.name: counterweight-weak-finding-survives
evals.prompt: sapiens mode. can you review this before I ship it? it's the auth token refresh we talked about
evals.expected_output: All three findings appear. The two strong ones lead. The third, weak but real, survives compression, because check 8 forbids dropping a finding to reach a length target.
assertions: Names the missing res.ok check
Names the concurrent-refresh race
Still mentions the undocumented REFRESH_WINDOW_MS constant and its coupling to the access token TTL
Reply is under 300 words
evals.baseline: Measured 2026-08: 252 words, all three findings present. The baseline passes this one. It is kept as a regression test, not as evidence the skill adds value here.

evals.name: status-question-after-a-failure
evals.prompt: sapiens mode. did the migration finish?
evals.expected_output: "No" in the first word. Then the half-migrated state, the reason re-running the whole file will not work, and the safe next step. The recommendation about making the migration re-runnable before production must survive, because it is a risk in a different environment and those go missing most often.
assertions: First word is No
States that staging is in a half-migrated state
States that re-running the whole file will fail
Still recommends making the migration idempotent or splitting it before production
Reply is under 200 words
evals.status: FAILING as of 3.7.0, after three measured attempts. Ships red on purpose. Do not relax the assertion to make it pass.
evals.baseline: Measured 2026-08: 254 words, and it volunteered the production recommendation unprompted. Skill 3.6.0 produced 118 words without it. Skill 3.7.0 produced 119 words, still without it, so sharpening check 8 did not fix this.
evals.diagnosis: Check 8 asks whether a finding was dropped between the draft and the final reply. Here it was never drafted: size discipline suppressed it at generation time, not at editing time, so there was nothing for check 8 to compare against. A check that runs on a finished draft cannot recover a thought that was never had. A second instance then turned up on the conversational probe c2, where the baseline recommended making an invasive fix its own revertible change and the skill dropped that advice. Two scenarios, same shape: advice attached to a moment other than now. Check 8 in 3.7.0 names that category. This eval stays red until a run shows the new wording actually changes the output, because a rule written in response to a failure is exactly the kind that looks right and does nothing.

evals.name: levels-change-detail-not-discipline
evals.prompt: Answer this three times, once at each level: /sapiens lead, then /sapiens dev, then /sapiens geek. The question is: the login flow sometimes rejects a valid login, what happened and is it fixed?
evals.expected_output: Three replies that differ in how much technical detail they carry, not in how disciplined they are. Lead names no files or functions. Dev explains the mechanism in plain words. Geek names the real symbols and the precise term. All three keep full grammar and stay inside the 25-word ceiling.
assertions: Lead version contains no file name, function name, or backticked symbol
Dev version explains the mechanism without requiring the term race condition
Geek version names at least one real symbol and uses the precise term
No sentence in any of the three exceeds 25 words
All three answer whether it is fixed within the first two sentences
evals.baseline: Not measured. The baseline has no concept of levels, so this eval tests the skill against itself for internal consistency.

evals.name: deferred-advice-survives-a-vague-followup
evals.prompt: sapiens mode. this is amazing, thank you so much!! honestly you saved my whole afternoon. what else could we improve here?
evals.expected_output: The four findings, ordered by what to do first. The advice attached to a later moment must survive: that the slowest fix is invasive and should be its own change so it is easy to revert.
assertions: Names all four findings
Orders them by what to do first
Still says the slow-fixture change should be done separately so it can be reverted
Reply is under 220 words
No sentence exceeds 25 words
evals.status: FAILING as of 3.7.0. Ships red, paired with eval 5.
evals.baseline: Measured 2026-08: 327 words. Named all four, ordered them, and volunteered the revert advice. Skill 3.7.0 produced 182 words with a new deferred-consequence warning about the URL bug, but without the revert advice.
evals.diagnosis: Second instance of the same failure as eval 5, in a different scenario. This is why check 8 names the category rather than the case.
